title: Looking Back in Time
question: How can anyone study the whole universe?
hook: Every telescope image of deep space is a picture of the past.
idea: Cosmology tests theories of the universe against light that has travelled for a very long time.

beats.prompt: In 1923 and 1924 Edwin Hubble found Cepheid variable stars in the Andromeda Galaxy and used them to find its distance. What did that show about spiral nebulae?

choices.label: They lie far beyond the edge of the Milky Way
They are clouds of gas inside the Milky Way
choices.feedback: Many thought so, but Andromeda's measured distance put it well outside our galaxy.

choices.label: They are too faint to measure at all
choices.feedback: Hubble did measure their distance, using the Cepheid stars.

beats.explain: Their distance placed spiral nebulae well beyond the Milky Way, resolving the Great Debate.

beats.prompt: Put these steps in cosmology in order.
items: Einstein publishes his cosmological paper on general relativity
Penzias and Wilson discover the microwave background
beats.explain: Newton's Principia came in 1687, Einstein's paper in 1917, Friedmann's idea in 1922 and the microwave background in 1964.

beats.prompt: Match each person to what they put forward.
beats.explain: Each idea moved cosmology forward from the one before.

beats.prompt: One step in this reasoning is wrong. Which?
steps: Light travels through space at a finite speed.
Light from a distant galaxy left it a long time ago.
So a telescope shows that galaxy exactly as it is today.
So looking out into space is looking back in time.
beats.explain: Because the light is old, the telescope shows the galaxy as it was, not as it is today.
